data.description:
## Description

What: Create the single-oracle corpus under tests/runners/fixtures/ covering the passing, RED-marker, and skipping axes. Each case is a fixture file plus a metadata record { id; verdict in {pass,fail,skip}; harnesses; description; drift_ticket? }. Add a schema that enforces the verdict vocabulary and rejects unknown tokens loudly, and a README at tests/runners/fixtures/ documenting the corpus and the metadata contract for downstream contributors. Why: This is the spine of the single-oracle model — without a canonical-verdict corpus and an enforced schema, no engine can be validated against an authority. Scope IN: fixture files across all three axes; the metadata schema and its loud-rejection behavior for malformed verdict tokens; the README contract. Scope OUT: the manifest (sc-2), the equivalence test harness (sc-3), regression snapshots (sc-6). Note: corpus is a protected hand-curated artifact and must be excluded from auto-remediation epics.

## Done Definitions

- tests/runners/fixtures/ contains at least one schema-valid case on each of the three axes (passing, RED-marker, skipping), each with a metadata record carrying id, verdict, harnesses, and description ← Satisfies: sc-1
- A metadata record whose verdict token is outside {pass,fail,skip} is rejected with a loud non-zero error rather than silently accepted ← Satisfies: sc-1
- A README at tests/runners/fixtures/ documents the corpus structure and the metadata schema as the contributor-facing contract ← Satisfies: sc-1

## Considerations

- [Boundary] tests/runners/** must be added to the plugin-boundary allowlist before first commit.
- [Governance] Tag/document the corpus as a protected hand-curated artifact so auto-remediation epics exclude it.
- [Shared-Contract] The corpus metadata 'harnesses' scope-annotation field MUST draw its identifier vocabulary from the draft-2 manifest (test-runners.yaml), which is the authoritative source of harness identifiers. The corpus references those identifiers rather than defining its own — otherwise draft-3's out-of-scope matching silently mis-keys against a divergent vocabulary.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a runner-contract maintainer, I want a schema-validated single-oracle fixture corpus with a documented metadata contract, so that every classification case carries one canonical verdict that engines can be checked against.
